title: Recoverable Releases Across Package Registries: A Git-Backed Saga Protocol
abstract: Releasing interdependent packages writes irreversibly to independent registries without a coordinator or rollback. A partial failure can therefore leave a consumer permanently behind a dependency that was published. This paper presents CCME, a commit-message language and release protocol for resumable releases, and dispat, its open-source implementation for single-package repositories, monorepos, and polyrepos joined through a control repository. In the formal model, release state consists of git tags, the plan is a pure function of repository history, dependency graph and configuration, and propagated work is admitted against the consumer's pending window. We prove eight guarantees, including no orphans, exactly-once ledger discharge and convergence under an explicit retry invariant. Minimal counterexamples establish why delivery must be tracked per consumer, why prerelease aggregation needs a separate window, and why retry guarantees require stable channel and suppression predicates. Against the official dispat 1.8.2 image, the fresh campaign passes six selected CCME 2.0 regressions, agrees with a restricted reference oracle on all 1,500 core instances, recovers 24/24 injected-failure episodes within four runs, and completes eight scale cells. The full profile intentionally generates regressive prereleases: 997 plans were accepted and 503 complete diagnostic plans were rejected with E195. All 1,914 differing rows retain their heuristic classification and stated coverage limits.
